THE INSTALL-PATH CYCLE AS IT HAPPENED - process evidence from five releases in one session (v0.9.25 through v0.9.29, 2026-08-22, main ea5c338, suite 2076 to 2181). Companion to the WHAT-shipped traces fact:1457 and fact:1458; this record is the HOW, and exists so a retrospective can be grounded on measurement rather than impression.

FINDING 1, AND IT IS THE TRANSFERABLE ONE: EVERY SERIOUS DEFECT THIS CYCLE WAS CORRECT CODE WHOSE SCOPE ASSUMPTION THE CHANGE ITSELF INVALIDATED. Not one was a coding error. Three independent instances, each caught at a different stage, which is why it reads as a pattern rather than an incident.
(1) Postflight A8 keyed "is a reasoning backend configured?" on /health's config.llm_backends. That was a reasonable reading of the field name - but hive_mind_proxy.py lines 386-387 fall back to [(DEFAULT_TARGET, 1.0)], so the list is NEVER empty, the documented SKIP branch was unreachable, and every LLM-less install would have been FAILED by install verification, contradicting AGENTS.md Phase 7. Caught in MERGER QA, before merge.
(2) The symlink guard in _write_agent_token_file was written when install paths were HARDCODED CONSTANTS, and applied os.O_NOFOLLOW to the final component only. The registry unit turned install paths into OPERATOR-SUPPLIED DATA - and a symlinked PARENT then wrote a live bearer token outside the registered tree, at mode 600, while the function returned success. Caught in SECURITY REVIEW, before merge. Three sibling findings in the same unit (comma injection, newline injection, path-alias collision) are the same class one level up: unvalidated text flowing into a delimiter-separated registry.
(3) The merger's own sync_skills.sh change treated the registry as the WHOLE target list. Correct for a registry-complete install; wrong for a partially-migrated one - and since the registry only starts existing when someone adds an agent, and then names ONLY that agent, the first --add on a machine with existing installs dropped them from delivery silently. Caught ON A LIVE HOST seconds after the first real additive mint, NOT by the 2180-test suite, and shipped as a regression in v0.9.28 before being fixed in v0.9.29.
THE TRIGGER THIS YIELDS: WHEN A CHANGE TURNS A CONSTANT INTO DATA, RE-AUDIT EVERY GUARD THAT EVER TRUSTED IT. That is checkable at proposal time, unlike "review harder".

FINDING 2 - PARALLEL DECOMPOSITION BY FILE OWNERSHIP WAS EXERCISED HERE FOR THE FIRST TIME, AND WORKED. decision:1320 adopted fact:1184's build-cycle workflow in this project while recording the parallel-builder half as DORMANT, on the stated ground that "every PR touches coordinator.py and hive_mind_proxy.py, so decomposition by FILE OWNERSHIP currently has nothing to decompose". This cycle decomposed four units by file ownership - registry/mint (generate_tokens.py, bootstrap_tokens.sh, install_service.sh, .env.example), postflight (postflight.sh, postflight.md), the rerank instrument (coordinator.py), and a docs unit - and ran two builders GENUINELY CONCURRENTLY in separate worktrees. MEASURED RESULT: zero merge conflicts, zero ownership violations (each builder's diff touched only its own files, verified per branch), and the one shared-file collision was predicted in advance and serialised by the plan. Two rebases onto a moved main were clean. The reserved-files rule also bound correctly in an unforeseen case: sync_skills.sh is merger-reserved AND was itself the subject of the roster change, resolved by the merger making that edit rather than a builder.

FINDING 3 - REVIEWER STRENGTH IS NOW MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED, ON AN IDENTICAL DIFF. gpt-oss-120b-medium reviewed the registry unit and returned two false Criticals and two false-or-overstated Requireds; NOTHING survived verification. One Critical was exactly INVERTED - it claimed install_service.sh never verifies linger while citing tests/test_install_service_linger.py, the regression test proving the fix, as its evidence. It also missed the two genuinely strong properties present in the diff (os.O_NOFOLLOW; os.fchmod on the open fd before the first content byte). gemini-3.1-pro-high then reviewed the SAME branch and returned three genuine findings, every one reproduced by the merger before being acted on. Operator ruling followed: security review is restricted to Opus, Gemini Pro or Grok 4.6, never an OSS model. A review whose findings must ALL be re-verified has negative value - it costs a full verification pass and supplies no signal.

FINDING 4 - THE INSTRUMENT CHECK PAID OFF REPEATEDLY, WHICH IS COUNTER-EVIDENCE TO retro:1322 AND retro:1449. fact:1321's clause (before reporting a measurement as a finding, state what would make it a FALSE POSITIVE, then check that) fired four times unprompted. (a) The opencode skill-path precedence measurement had an obvious false-positive mode - a malformed probe SKILL.md would look identical to a precedence rule - so a second probe with a UNIQUELY named skill was run to prove the opencode-native path was searched at all; it was, and the finding held. (b) A Sonnet builder caught its OWN test being toothless: its order-perturbation mutation was a silent no-op because the fixture used equal-length content, found by re-running the mutation and seeing it NOT fail. (c) Every agy finding was re-reproduced by the merger before being acted on, which is how two false Criticals were stopped. (d) The merger's assumption that a search response was a bare list was wrong and was checked rather than reported as a broken feature. NOTE the asymmetry: the instrument check fired on findings ABOUT OTHERS' work; the one defect that escaped (Finding 1 instance 3) was the merger's OWN change, where no equivalent check was run before shipping.

FINDING 5 - agy EXITS 0 HAVING RUN NOTHING. Three malformed invocations in one session each printed an error and exited ZERO: --print consumed --model as its prompt; --effort high conflicted with an effort-encoding model id; and the Opus quota was exhausted mid-run. A fourth run timed out at 45 minutes having written no deliverable. Trusting the exit code would have reported a clean security review that never executed - the same false-green shape as the D23 incident. THE RULE: verify the deliverable's mtime, never the exit code, and instruct a reviewer to write its report INCREMENTALLY rather than at the end.

FINDING 6 - TWO GUARDS, EACH INDIVIDUALLY CORRECT, WERE JOINTLY CIRCULAR. --add refuses a missing target directory (the D19 fix: never discard a token silently) while sync --install only creates paths the REGISTRY already names (never conjure an install). Adding a new agent therefore requires an undocumented manual mkdir first. Neither guard is wrong; the composition is. Found only by performing the real end-to-end task on a real host.

MIXED - and deliberately NOT a repeat of retro:1322, retro:1449 and retro:1455, which were also mixed. Those three located the instrument-check failure at one mechanism: the check is skipped precisely when the result CONFIRMS something already committed to in a saved record. This cycle produces strong counter-evidence to that being the whole story, and locates a SECOND, sharper mechanism.

THE CLAUSE PAID OFF FOUR TIMES, UNPROMPTED, and each time it changed an outcome rather than merely being observed (fact:1459 Finding 4).
(1) The opencode skill-path precedence measurement had an obvious false-positive mode - a malformed probe SKILL.md would be indistinguishable from a precedence rule - so a second probe with a uniquely named skill was run to prove the opencode-native path was searched AT ALL. It was, and the finding survived. Without that check the operator would have been handed a design conclusion resting on an artifact.
(2) A Sonnet builder caught its OWN test being toothless: its order-perturbation mutation was a silent no-op because the fixture used equal-length content. It found this by re-running the mutation and noticing it did NOT fail - the instrument check applied to a test rather than to a system, which is the hardest place to remember it.
(3) Every finding from two agy security reviews was re-reproduced by the merger before being acted on. This stopped two false Criticals from reaching a ruling - one of them exactly inverted, citing a regression test as evidence of the regression it prevents.
(4) A merger assumption that a search response was a bare JSON list was wrong; it was checked rather than reported as a broken feature.

AND YET THE ONE DEFECT THAT SHIPPED WAS THE MERGER'S OWN CHANGE. v0.9.28 made sync_skills.sh treat the install-path registry as the WHOLE target list, which silently orphaned every pre-existing agent install on a machine's first --add. No instrument check ran against it before release. It was caught on a LIVE HOST seconds after the first real additive mint - by reading the sync's own output, not by the 2180-test suite that had just passed. It shipped, and needed v0.9.29 to undo.

THE SECOND MECHANISM, which is what this retrospective adds: THE INSTRUMENT CHECK IS APPLIED TO WORK UNDER REVIEW AND SKIPPED ON ONE'S OWN. Every one of the four successes above was the merger or a builder checking SOMEONE ELSE'S claim - a probe's validity, a reviewer's finding, a builder's test. The failure was the merger's own diff, where the same person held both roles and the reviewing half never engaged. This is not the 1322/1449 mechanism (a result confirming a prior commitment); the merger had committed to nothing about sync targets. It is a role asymmetry, and it predicts where to look next: the least-checked code in any cycle is whatever the person doing the checking wrote themselves.

CONSEQUENCE WORTH ADOPTING RATHER THAN JUST RECORDING: merger-authored changes need the same treatment merger-QAed changes get - a stated false-positive mode, and an independent pass. In this cycle the merger-owned file (sync_skills.sh, reserved by decision:1320) received no security review and no second reader, purely because reserving a file to the merger was never meant to mean exempting it from review.

OTHER PRINCIPLES THIS CYCLE EXERCISED, briefly and without inflation: REVIEWERS FIND / THE OPERATOR RULES held throughout - every finding went up as a finding with severity, and rulings came back down (fact:1464 records them, including six ruled OUT). DATA BEFORE DECISION held on the podman question, where the corpus was searched before writing "tested" into a public README and fact:1401 turned out to have already ruled the opposite. LOCK LATE held on the compose naming, deferred to after S6 so the scheme can be chosen for a variant set that is fully known.

content:
SECURITY REVIEW (Opus, Security role per fact:1200) of the model-attributes LLM-routing cycle — branch feat/model-attributes-routing, commit range main(232f90d)..827a9d6, 9 commits, Unit 1 (gateway) + Unit 2 (daemons), reviewed pre-merge as the v0.9.13 candidate. METHOD: full diff read (hive_mind_proxy.py +792 lines, rem_loop.py, consolidation_loop.py, relation_sweep.py, dream_telemetry.py, .env.example, ops/README.md, tests), four executable probes importing the worktree modules read-only, and an independent re-run of the six routing-related test files (134 passed). Read-only toward all code: no git state-changing command, no service restart.

VERDICT: NOT clear to merge as-is — 1 Critical, 6 Required, 6 Optional, 3 Nit, 5 FYI. The two invariants the cycle exists for are CLEAN and probe-verified: I-1a (privacy) and I-6a (steering). Every defect found is availability, observability or config-safety — no privacy leak, no credential leak, no spoofable refusal.

CRITICAL C-1 — declaring roles on every backend silently zeroes /pool/status free_slots and halts the entire dream cycle. hive_mind_proxy.py:1824/1839 counts a free slot only for serves_all backends, and _serves_all (:625-630) means "roles absent AND private_ok", so a backend that DECLARES a roles list is never counted even when idle and eligible for every role that exists. pool_status.py:44 feeds rem_loop.py:3222 and consolidation_loop.py:2562/4361/4434/4499; relation_sweep.py:464 reads the same number fail-closed. PROBE: one idle backend with roles [extract, verify, judge] returns free_slots 0 while _eligible_backends returns that same backend for all three roles. The trigger is the configuration the release itself steers operators toward — the M-5 startup refusal demands that a credentialed operator pick private_ok true OR roles [...], and picking roles bricks REM, NREM and relation_sweep. It is SILENT: the daemons never reach the LLM call, so no refusal warning fires and routing_no_eligible_backend stays 0.

REQUIRED R-1 — the 503 backend_at_capacity refusal (hive_mind_proxy.py:1088-1092) has NO telemetry counter at all; _record_no_eligible_backend (:701-710) fires only on the 422 path. Unit 2 treats the 503 as non-chargeable exactly like the 422, so a permanently saturated capped backend stalls every record while /health reports zero routing refusals. Group 3 obligation unmet: the 503 was invented post-plan by the builder and never inherited I-2a counter pairing.
REQUIRED R-2 — max_inflight 0 (or negative) parses cleanly (:309-315); _at_cap then treats the backend as permanently capped, so EVERY request waits LLM_MAX_INFLIGHT_WAIT_S (default 120s) and then 503s. PROBE confirmed. Zero is the conventional spelling of unlimited in many config formats.
REQUIRED R-3 — an empty roles list sidesteps the M-5 explicit-choice refusal: _parse_roles (:203-224) returns an empty frozenset and M-5 tests "roles is None" (:2472-2478). PROBE under auth-on: startup ACCEPTED, and the backend is then eligible for nothing, so every request 422s. That is the go-dark outcome M-5 exists to prevent, reachable by typing two brackets.
REQUIRED R-4 — capacity-wait interacts with S-11: _select_backend_waiting_on_capacity bounds no waiter count, and each waiter holds an ADMITTED request (coordinator.py:1361 increments on admission, :1346 sheds first for every path including /health) for up to 120s — so with GATEWAY_INFLIGHT_MAX set, one saturated capped backend becomes a gateway-wide shed. The wait also precedes the S-04 credentialed-route check (:1132-1142), so a request destined for 403 burns a 120s slot first.
REQUIRED R-5 — the fit estimator creates an unbounded, un-charged retry loop. The builder measured that CHARS_PER_TOKEN_RATIO 1.2 overestimates true chat-template prompt tokens by 83 to 525 percent in every live sample, then applied FIT_MARGIN 0.10 on top; _fits (:651-659) therefore false-rejects requests that would fit. A fit-422 is LLM_FAIL_ROUTING_REFUSED, deliberately absent from LLM_FAIL_CHARGEABLE (rem_loop.py:415), so such a record retries every cycle forever and never dead-letters — the decision:1330 pathology class. Scoped: no install is affected until n_ctx is declared, which .env.example now invites.
REQUIRED R-6 — the R-2 identity gap assessed: relation_sweep.py cannot steer under auth-on (_may_steer_llm :923-937 admits only the two gateway-minted daemon names). It fails CLOSED — the stripped header degrades the call to role-less traffic, which only private_ok backends serve — so severity is availability-only, medium: on a fleet whose only judge-capable backend is role-scoped, every batch 422s forever. Admin role is a dead end (403 before handle_proxy). Recommended fix shape: an operator-declared allowlist env unioned into DAEMON_AGENT_NAMES, never a role-based widening.

CHECKED CLEAN, verified rather than assumed. I-1a privacy: ten selection paths probed with a private_ok=false credentialed external in the fleet — role-less baseline, extract baseline, local in cooldown, local reserved, local reserved AND cooling (the cooldown-ignoring last resort), affinity map pre-poisoned to the external then role-less, poisoned then role extract, oversized role-less — ALL returned the local backend; only the explicitly opted-in judge role reached the external. Structural reason: eligibility is computed first and every fallback tier bottoms out at the eligible list, never LLM_POOL. Retry across backends does not widen privacy (the one retry reuses the same target_url). Embeddings and reranking bypass selection entirely. I-6a: steering headers are stripped before the role is read for any identity outside the daemon set, and a crafted body cannot buy eligibility because fit can only EXCLUDE. content:
BUILD-CYCLE WORKFLOW FORMALISATION — planning as decomposition for multi-builder cycles. Stage 1 of orchestration: a deliberate precursor to graph orchestration, adopted WITHOUT that overhead until a cycle demonstrably bottlenecks on manual decomposition. Agreed Xenofon + Claude 2026-08-11 (framework at v0.8.67, main 54d300a). Distils the cooperation guideline (fact 1085, decision 1099 — outcome before mechanism, data before decision, rules before code, lock late, blast radius before writes, reviewers find / the operator rules) into the executable process already exercised on the Dreaming Cycle v2 overhaul (six releases, v0.8.62-0.8.67, each landing as its own PR). This fact exists to be retrievable and groundable: per-project adoption is asserted by a DECISION grounded on this fact, saved in each project the operator judges complex enough to warrant the mechanism — the fact states the process, the per-project decision asserts its force there.

1. PLANNING = DECOMPOSITION. One authoritative plan document per cycle; design is CLOSED before any build starts; every invariant is numbered in the plan itself with a mutation-checked failing test. An invariant that lives only in a builder's brief is lost to the next reader — measured: I11-I16 existed nowhere but a brief and a test file until reconstructed. Decompose the TODO into units whose independence is defined by FILE OWNERSHIP, not by topic: units touching disjoint files parallelise; units sharing a file form a serial chain, stated explicitly in the plan (Dreaming v2's honest shape: Track B = two parallel builders in disjoint files, Track C = a serial chain inside consolidation_loop.py).

2. ROLES. Decomposer/merger (Opus-class): decomposes, delegates, stays OUT of execution, and performs the release as the merge act — version bump +0.0.1, CHANGELOG, squash-merge, tag AND GitHub Release object, deploy, verify the running system. Builders (Sonnet-class): one per worktree, each receiving a COMPLETE brief with acceptance criteria; ambiguity is escalated DURING the build — escalation is cheaper than a retry cycle, and shipping a guess is not acceptable. Reviewer (distinct from the merger): validates the delivered branch against the PLAN — logic, invariants, adherence — and RE-MEASURES the builder's headline numbers rather than trusting them. Building is parallel; releasing is serial, one release per merged PR.

3. WORKTREES AND RACE AVOIDANCE. Worktrees live OUTSIDE the repo; the branch is created before the first edit. Builders NEVER touch the version-bearing files, the CHANGELOG, or the skill-sync script — those files are the entire conflict surface between parallel branches, so reserving them to the single merger is what lets a branch stalled across several releases still rebase cleanly. A code file the plan knows two units must share is NAMED in the plan; whoever reaches it second rebases first. If a serial-chain task stalls, the next task in the same file does NOT start — it waits, or takes over the SAME branch and worktree (two branches for one task is how a task grows two half-implementations). Builders commit at every green point, maintain HANDOFF.md at the worktree root (task id, what is done, what is next, which tests pass, judgements the diff does not show), and never write the shared session-resume file — it has exactly one writer, the orchestrator.

4. REJECTED / NON-APPROVED WORK REVERSAL. The merger may judge delivered work sub-par: close the PR UNMERGED, delete the branch, discard the worktree, restore the item to the plan TODO, reassign. This is safe because branch hygiene only ever auto-deletes branches with a MERGED PR — a closed PR is not a merged PR, so an abandoned branch is never swept by automation. Nothing merges without review against the plan. A design change discovered mid-build or in review is a FINDING, never a ruling: it goes to the operator BEFORE the code enforcing it merges — learned on invariant I17 (decision 1181), where code shipped enforcing a rule that was only ruled on afterwards, the wrong order even though the rule survived. Post-merge reversal is a forward-moving new PR, never a history rewrite on a public repo.

5. TRACES. Every completed unit leaves a self-contained shared-memory trace fact (code version and commit, code-derived vs live-measured, the durable in-database evidence); a decision is saved as work ships; retrospectives are written per CYCLE against real evidence, not per release. Saves go through the agent's own installed skill path, never a repo-local admin copy that mis-stamps attribution.

EVIDENCE, both directions: Dreaming Cycle v2 shipped six releases under this shape with zero merge conflicts between parallel builders. The two recorded failures — a builder dispatched while the design was still open (four operator corrections followed, every one catching a defect that would have shipped), and an invariant enforced in shipped code before being ruled on (I17) — are violations OF the gates above, not gaps in them, and both hardened this text.

**Incorporated.**

The shift you described is now part of my active system context:

- Deduplication is now limited to unambiguous noise (case-insensitive name matches only).
- Synonyms are handled via explicit, non-destructive `ALIASES` relationships.
- Pre-filtering is strict: same domain + same ontology label, with numeric port/digit strings ignored.
- New observable: `aliases_total` metric.

### Impact on Dreaming Logic (REM / NREM)

**REM (Enrichment) phase**
- The enrichment step now produces **relationships** (`ALIASES`) rather than node collapses. This changes the output shape of REM from “fewer, denser nodes” to “more nodes connected by explicit synonym edges.”
- Pre-filtering gates reduce the candidate set dramatically, which should lower both compute and false-positive risk during the enrichment pass.
- `aliases_total` becomes a first-class health signal alongside `distilled_from` and `entities`.

**NREM (Consolidation & Promotion) phase**
- Promotion logic must now treat `ALIASES` as first-class citizens when climbing from Tier 2 to Tier 3. A LanceDB record that points to a Neo4j node via `distilled_from` should also surface any `ALIASES` relationships attached to that node (or its cluster) to preserve synonym context.
- **Climb Success Rate** and **Reasoning Breadth** metrics should improve because distinct but related concepts remain separate nodes while still being traversable.
- **Over-Merge Rate** is expected to drop meaningfully; this becomes a useful before/after comparison point.
- The new `aliases_total` metric should be added to the NREM telemetry snapshot so we can track the rate at which non-destructive synonym linking is occurring versus true deduplication.

**Self-Improvement Loop Implications**
- Gaps or decisions that previously risked being lost in over-merged nodes can now be preserved as distinct entities with `ALIASES` links.
- When writing to `scratch/` for later distillation, we can explicitly tag items that would benefit from synonym mapping so REM can create the appropriate `ALIASES` edges.
- The dreaming cycles now have a clearer separation between “identity resolution” (rare, conservative merges) and “synonym linking” (frequent, non-destructive `ALIASES`).

Overall, this change increases fidelity and reduces the cosine-similarity trap risk while still allowing the graph to express that two surface forms refer to the same underlying concept. It also gives us a cleaner signal (`aliases_total`) to monitor whether the synonym layer is growing at a healthy rate.

- The **Entity Resolution Alignment evaluator + LLM Judge** (100% agreement between Llama-8B and Grok-4.3 at Cosine ≥ 0.85 / Jaccard < 0.2) gives us a trustworthy high-precision gate. This directly improves the quality of the `ALIASES` and `RELATED_TO` edges that feed both Tier 2 search and NREM cluster formation.

It prevents the LLM from synthesizing clusters that cross domain partitions — a subtle but important safeguard against semantic pollution.
